page: Google Cloud Platform c2d-highcpu-8 is a compute-optimized virtual machine instance powered by an AMD EPYC 7B13 processor. Utilizing the x86_64 architecture, this instance features 8 vCPUs mapped to 4 physical cores with 2 threads per core under a dedicated CPU allocation model. It is configured with 16 GB of system memory, yielding a resource density of 2.0 GB of RAM per vCPU. The processor includes 32 KB of L1d cache, 0.5 MB of L2 cache, and 32 MB of L3 cache. It supports hardware-accelerated instruction sets such as AVX, AES, VAES, SHA_NI, and FMA, though it lacks AVX-512 capabilities. No local storage or GPU accelerators are bundled with this instance.

Benchmark evaluations indicate strong single-core CPU performance, with stress-ng single-core tests placing the instance in the top 25% of its class. Multi-core CPU performance, Geekbench scores, and Passmark CPU metrics generally fall within the average range. Memory bandwidth is also average, measuring 68.67 GB/sec for large-block read operations and 49.73 GB/sec for large-block write operations. A notable performance tradeoff is observed in multi-threaded bzip3 decompression, which registers in the bottom 25% of tested systems. Static web serving throughput is measured at an average rate of 10.6 GB/sec, and small-model LLM inference achieves 569.63 tokens/sec for prompt processing.

From a qualitative cost-efficiency perspective, the c2d-highcpu-8 offers a lean memory-to-vCPU ratio designed to minimize overhead costs for compute-bound tasks that do not require large memory footprints. The dedicated CPU allocation ensures consistent execution times, making it suitable for workloads such as software compilation, web serving, and moderate computational tasks. However, the lack of local storage and GPU accelerators limits its utility for large-scale database hosting or deep learning workloads. It is best suited for compute-heavy applications, web servers, and lightweight batch processing.
